function: Joint AAV 2D placement and per-user power allocation learned by DDPG and SAC actors, hybrid beamforming analytical, maximizing total harvested power under rate and power thresholds (p. 10)
system: BS and AAV relay with 144 antennas each (hybrid beamforming), K single-antenna IoT users, decode-and-forward half-duplex relay; 28 GHz, 500 MHz; no RIS (p. 5, p. 10)
method: Off-policy actor-critic DRL (DDPG-AD, SAC-AD), two-hidden-layer MLPs; state is AAV position, action is position step plus softmax power split; transfer learning across topologies (p. 10, p. 16)
data_channel: Custom Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel (10 paths, path-loss exponent 3.6), 100x100 m area, randomly placed users; simulated, no dataset or measurement (p. 6, p. 10, p. 11)
test_conditions: Fixed topologies with K=3 (narrow or wide clusters); K=6 case trained on l1, networks transferred to l2 and l3, evaluated for PT 0-50 dBm (p. 13, p. 16)
baselines: Non-learned: PSO-AD, user-centroid UA-AD, fixed-position F-AD, equal power allocation. Learned: only the paper's own DDPG-AD and SAC-AD; no external learned method compared (p. 13, p. 15)
metrics: Total harvested power (dBm), achievable rate (bps/Hz), per-user thresholds, accumulated reward, online runtime in ms (p. 13, p. 14, p. 17)
complexity: Big-O orders for HBF, PSO-AD, and DDPG/SAC training and inference; K=2 runtime 3.65 ms (DDPG-AD), 7.69 ms (SAC-AD) vs 549.6 ms (PSO-AD) (p. 16, p. 17)
q1_support: p. 6: "per the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model" - custom clustered geometric mmWave simulator (Table 2, p. 10); no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measurement is used.
q2_support: p. 16: "both agents achieve faster convergence" - networks trained on user distribution l1 are transferred to the new distributions l2 and l3 and adapt in fewer episodes than full retraining.
q3_support: p. 13: "proposed DRL schemes are evaluated against three baseline" - the baselines PSO-AD, UA-AD and F-AD are non-learned; DDPG-AD and SAC-AD are both the paper's own schemes, so no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 17: "The online complexity of inference" - Section V-E gives big-O training and inference costs, and p. 17 gives measured runtimes against PSO-AD.
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulation parameters are summarized in Table 2." - the paper uses its own simulator; no code or data link, DOI or public dataset appears in the 19 pages.
notes: Area 6: aerial relay link with learned AAV placement and power allocation; the hybrid beamforming is analytical (p. 7-8), so area 3 does not apply. Passes above_phy because power allocation is learned jointly with placement. q3 is borderline: DDPG-AD and SAC-AD are both proposed and the paper names only three non-learned baselines (p. 13); the reviewer may instead count DDPG-AD as a standard-algorithm baseline for SAC-AD. q2 rests on transfer from l1 to l2 and l3 (p. 16). Tables 1-3 were read from page images (p. 4, p. 10, p. 13). The DOI on p. 18 is an earlier conference version, not code or data.
